change: Borrow Execution retirement tables once per batch and reuse each object-family read; return after call validation for an empty batch.

contract.before: Repeated private RefCell borrows and object-family reads for each object; table/removal/finalization ordering as defined by Execution.
contract.after: The same loops, lookups, removals and fallible operations use batch-scoped private borrows. Family is read once while its owner table is unchanged. An empty batch skips effect-free cleanup.
review: Machine and continuation engine finalization and retire_owned make no language calls and do not mutate the Objects table; its borrow spans no callbacks.
Removed table values have no language-calling destructors. Rust allocation/refcount cleanup stays inside the same owner.
Per-object finalization/removal order and early error propagation remain unchanged. Owner context and argument-slice validation still precede the empty return.
All payload interpretation remains with Execution. Id, lookup, scheduler budgets and GC policy are unchanged.

retirement_microbenchmark.scope: Existing Execution retire: on live, retained, zero-payload Id objects not owned by Execution. Measures rejection/cleanup work for unrelated entries, not full GC. Captured Block and unrelated allocation identities verified unchanged.

full_collection.scope: Full precise collection after 1000 Integer/Range iterations; automatic GC disabled only while producing garbage, same policy in both lanes. Six collection timings per variant, two fresh processes, ABBA. Successful nonempty collections checked.
full_collection.interpretation: Changes below 1% in opposite directions do not establish a whole-GC speedup. The demonstrated gain is the retirement subroutine.

validation: 24 Execution unit tests in the core gate.
Full Oop core/compiler/GC suite, including negative dispatch/construction and retirement/finalizer failures.
Method/Machine lifetime, continuation transparency, native incoming calls, closure admission and pending-call recovery.
Added an empty-retirement check that rejects an invalid Method context.
limits: The retirement microbenchmark uses retained objects not owned by Execution, reproducing the unrelated-object work without freeing them. It is not a substitute for the full collection and lifetime checks.
Six fresh processes per microbenchmark variant, five samples per size in each. A first shorter comparison was variable, so alternating repetitions were extended before retention.
Only the rebuilt Execution library is substituted into the previous prefix; no installed user runtime or generated image is replaced.
No timing threshold; local CPU measurements are not universal guarantees.
